newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Elan says Q2 trading encouraging so far.
newsitem.headline: Elan says Q2 trading encouraging so far.

text.p: Irish-based pharmaceutical group Elan Corp Plc said on Monday that trading in the second quarter had so far been encouraging.

"For the second quarter we are reasonably encouraged that we will be in line with good expectations," executive vice president and chief financial officer Thomas Lynch told reporters in Dublin at a briefing about the company.
"The key thing for the quarter and for the year is how our drugs are doing," Lynch said.

"Permax continues to sell very well, and Zanaflex, which we launched in February, has been very well received by the neurology community and is building market share," he said. "The principle drug delivery products Naprelan, Cardizem and Verelan are all on track."
In April, Elan reported first-quarter net income of $37.2 million and earnings per share of $0.36, compared with $28.6 million and $0.35 in the same period in 1996.
